BiblicalUsage: The ayah is a bird of prey — the kite or hawk, named among the unclean birds Israel must not eat. Leviticus and Deuteronomy both list it after its kind, and Job says there is a path no bird of prey knows, not even the eye of the vulture has seen it, speaking of the hidden way to wisdom.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that even an unclean bird can teach me something: the hawk's eye misses the path to wisdom entirely. Only God knows where it lies.
